answer: Require every agent to hold one PADI Open Water Diver certification, verified against PADI's diver lookup by certification number and full name. The course costs about $450 and demands four supervised open-water dives across three days, so a forger wanting 1,000 fake agents faces 1,000 in-person courses and $450,000 before one puppet reaches the market — a scheme that hits its nadir the moment one card is checked. An ivory counterfeit fails the name match, a pigment-printed forgery means nothing without a matching registry row, and the identity is rejected.
